Tech stocks were higher late Wednesday afternoon with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rising 0.6% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) up 0.4%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index advanced 1.5%.

In corporate news, Oracle (ORCL) shares rose more than 11% after it reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 outlook and set long-term targets at its Investor Day on Wednesday, including FY30 revenue of $225 billion or more.

The US Department of Justice is examining how Nvidia's (NVDA) planned $12.93 billion acquisition of Hugging Face could affect competition in the AI sector, Reuters reported. Nvidia shares were down 1.5%.

OpenAI is planning to buy AI computing chips from Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google to help build its infrastructure, The Information reported. Alphabet shares rose 1.3%.

Dropbox (DBX) is cutting about 9% of its global workforce. The company estimates the reduction will result in cash expenditures of $27 million to $33 million, primarily for severance payments, employee benefits and related costs. The company's shares fell 1.3%.

title: Oracle shares jump as long-term outlook targets $225 billion in revenue
detail:
Oracle shares jump as long-term outlook targets $225 billion in revenue
Louis Juricic
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 3:03 PM EDT 2 min read
ORCL
Trade Oracle on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Oracle shares rose 8.6% Wednesday after the company laid out an ambitious long-term growth plan, projecting annual revenue of at least $225 billion by fiscal 2030 while promising to rein in capital spending and limit additional financing needs.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The cloud software and infrastructure company expects revenue to grow at a compound annual rate of more than 35% from fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2030, according to its investor-day presentation. Oracle also forecast non-GAAP earnings per share of at least $21 and a non-GAAP operating margin of at least 40% by fiscal 2030.

The outlook offers investors a longer-term view of how Oracle expects to turn its expanding artificial intelligence infrastructure business into sustained earnings and cash flow, as the company invests heavily to meet demand for computing capacity.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Oracle expects capital expenditures to peak in fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 before declining in fiscal 2029. It also projects positive free cash flow in the second half of fiscal 2028, rising to at least $30 billion in fiscal 2029.

The company said it expects growth to become self-funded beginning in fiscal 2029, with net debt to adjusted EBITDA falling below 3.5 times that year. Oracle also plans to limit additional capital-market funding through fiscal 2030 to $20 billion, split evenly between equity and gross debt, excluding refinancing of existing debt.

That financing plan comes after Oracle completed a $20 billion at-the-market equity offering in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, highlighting the scale of the capital required to support its infrastructure expansion.

Oracle reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 outlook, calling for revenue of at least $90 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $8.10.

(Bloomberg) -- Oracle Corp. gave a long-term outlook for free cash flow that was better than analysts' estimates, easing investor nerves about the potential payoff from its artificial intelligence spending.

Free cash flow will be $30 billion in the fiscal year ending in May 2029, Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said Wednesday during the company's annual conference in Las Vegas. Investors had expected free cash flow to remain negative in that year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Oracle, long known for its database software, has been working to refashion itself as a provider of computing power for AI work and is embarking on a major build-out of data centers for OpenAI and other customers. Wall Street is closely watching the scale of spending on these ambitious projects and how quickly Oracle can complete them.

The shares jumped as much as 9.6% on the company's long-range forecast. The stock had dropped 33% this year through Tuesday's close.

title: Oracle Investor Day 2026: Accelerating Value Creation
detail:
This is a paid press release. Contact the press release distributor directly with any inquiries.
Oracle Investor Day 2026: Accelerating Value Creation
PR Newswire
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 2:21 PM EDT 5 min read
ORCL
Trade Oracle on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Set long-term outlook for FY30 of $225 billion+ in total revenue, representing more than 35% CAGR from FY26, non-GAAP operating margin of 40%+ and non-GAAP EPS $21+.

Defined timeline to positive free cash flow during the second half of FY28 and set free cash flow target of $30 billion+ for FY29.

Committed to limiting additional capital raises through FY30 to $20 billion, excluding refinancing of existing debt, split between $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in gross debt.

Confirmed that growth will be self-funded beginning in FY29 and net debt to adjusted EBITDA will be below 3.5 times in FY29.1

AUSTIN, Texas, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle Corporation (NYSE: ORCL) today hosted an Investor Day in Las Vegas, NV. At the event co-CEO Clay Magouryk, co-CEO Mike Sicilia and CFO Hilary Maxson presented and responded to questions about the company's strategy and updated medium-term financial guidance.

Accelerating Shareholder Value throughout the FY27-FY30 Investment Cycle

At its Investor Day, Oracle described how its unique portfolio positioning across cloud infrastructure, database and applications is expected to drive total revenue growth of more than 35% CAGR from FY26 through FY30, reaching total revenue of $225 billion or more in FY30. It also outlined its expectations for strong profitability and free cash flow generation from each of its three business models. Following a period of peak capex in FY27-FY28, capital expenditures are expected to step-down in FY29, supporting positive free cash flow of at least $30 billion in FY29.

Oracle committed to limiting additional funding to be raised in the capital markets for its FY27-FY30 investment cycle to $20 billion, currently expected to be $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in gross debt. This incremental funding requirement excludes refinancing of existing debt. This is in addition to the $20 billion at-the-market equity raise completed in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Vendor financing, customer-provided hardware and customer prepayments are expected to reduce upfront cash requirements through the transition to positive free cash flow.

Oracle reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 outlook for total revenue of at least $90 billion and non-GAAP earnings per share of $8.10. The company's capital allocation priorities remain maintaining investment-grade credit ratings, paying a dividend and funding growth opportunities.

The Investor Day presentations and webcast replay will be available on the Oracle Investor Day website.

1. Net debt includes borrowings, vendor financing, and operating and finance lease liabilities, less cash and marketable securities. Adjusted EBITDA is based on Oracle's reported non-GAAP results, with depreciation and operating lease expense added back.

title: Is Oracle Stock Worth Buying as Autonomous Database Use Keeps Growing?
detail:
Is Oracle Stock Worth Buying as Autonomous Database Use Keeps Growing?
Vasundhara Sawalka
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 12:39 PM EDT 3 min read
ORCL
MSFT
SNOW
MDB
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Oracle Corporation ORCL is turning its Autonomous AI Database into a key channel for monetizing enterprise AI demand, and its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results indicate that adoption is broadening well beyond Oracle Cloud Infrastructure ("OCI").

In the quarter ended Aug. 31, 2026, cloud database revenues rose 26% to $0.9 billion, while multicloud database revenues, generated by Oracle database services running inside Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services, soared 353% year over year. This contributed to cloud infrastructure revenues of $7.4 billion, up 121%, and total revenues of $19.3 billion, up 30%. Remaining performance obligations reached $664 billion, up $209 billion year over year.

October 2026 announcements at Oracle AI World extend this reach. Oracle added a business semantic layer and expanded Apache Iceberg support for Autonomous AI Lakehouse. ORCL launched Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud in Mexico, taking availability to 17 Google Cloud regions, and unveiled its Deep Trust AI Architecture, built around Autonomous AI Database's automated security patching. A new OpenAI collaboration links Oracle App Composer to Autonomous AI Database, creating another entry point for AI workloads.

Guidance supports the growth narrative. For second-quarter fiscal 2027, Oracle expects total revenue growth of 30-34% and cloud revenue growth of 65-71% in U.S. dollars. For fiscal 2027, it projects revenues of at least $90 billion, up 34% in constant currency, and non-GAAP earnings of $8.10 per share.

However, risks remain. Database revenues are modest compared with the $6.5 billion CPU and GPU infrastructure business. Capital expenditure jumped to $28.5 billion in the quarter, though net cash outlay was $18 billion. Free cash flow was negative $5.4 billion, and a $20 billion common stock sale dilutes shareholders.

Overall, autonomous database momentum, expanding multicloud reach and raised guidance make Oracle an appealing long-term holding, though cash flow and funding needs warrant close monitoring.

How Snowflake and MongoDB Compare in Cloud Database Growth

Oracle faces competition from Snowflake SNOW and MongoDB MDB in cloud data management. Snowflake's second-quarter fiscal 2027 product revenues rose 37% year over year to $1.49 billion, while its net revenue retention rate was 126%. Snowflake raised its fiscal 2027 product revenue outlook to $6.07 billion, implying 36% growth. MongoDB's second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues increased 30% to $771.8 million, with its Atlas cloud database growing about 29% and contributing roughly 73% of total revenue. MongoDB ended the quarter with more than 70,600 customers and expects fiscal 2027 revenues of $2.99-$3.03 billion. Both Snowflake and MongoDB continue reporting consumption-led gains.
